*** SPRINT 74 / V0.29.29 -- US-540-a DONE code-side. 2 of 6 (US-539, US-540-a). Next up: US-540-b (re-lay the card set 4->6, Health retires). ***

THE SCALE IS NOW 44/34/26/20/15 in specs/UI/tokens.css + the dashboard.css :root mirror. That was the entire change: ten value lines and two comment blocks, nothing below :root. US-539 was built to make this exact edit small and it did -- the pre-F-127 panel would have needed 82 edits and they would have drifted.

*** DO NOT READ THE GREEN SUITE AS ACCEPTANCE. Two things are still owed and NEITHER is closable on a dev box: acceptance is IN-CAR seated at arm's length, and AC2 requires the OUTPUT MODE be confirmed panel-native BEFORE these numbers are called final. That confirmation is US-552, still open in this sprint. If the Pi is pushing 1080p into a 480x320 panel, every glyph is scale-up-then-downsampled soft and the real floor is ABOVE 34px -- so the correct order is US-552, then read the panel, then ratify or move the five numbers. A browser on Windows cannot see the defect that AC exists to catch. ***

EYEBALL IN THIS ORDER ON HARDWARE: (1) the STOP 'PULL OVER NOW' directive -- US-539 already forced it 22->40 and hero is now 44; at 40px mono it was ~340px of 442px available, so it is the likeliest line to wrap/clip and it is a SAFETY surface. (2) any 4-fact card -- secondary went 14->26, the biggest proportional jump in the scale (+86%). OVERFLOW SEEN NOW IS US-540-b's PROBLEM (that story re-lays the cards to ~3 facts each), NOT a reason to shrink the scale back -- shrinking is F-127 travelling backwards. (3) meta 10->15 furniture (version chip, IMU tape): the one tier where growth costs layout and buys little, since it is parked-read micro-copy.

*** THE GENERALIZABLE LESSON FROM THE GATE: PIN VALUES, DON'T BOUND THEM, WHEN THE VALUES ARE THE DELIVERABLE. My first instinct was a floor test ('primary >= 34') -- it is the AC's own words. But that test would have PASSED BEFORE THIS STORY RAN (the old hero was 40 and would have cleared any hero floor), and it would still pass if a later edit pushed hero to 90px and overflowed every card. A bound cannot witness a value; only a pin can. I pinned the five numbers AND asserted the intent separately (floor / non-critical-ceiling / no-tier-shrank) so the WHY survives the next value edit. ***

Also pinned: no tier smaller than its pre-F-127 value, because an overflow fix under deadline is exactly how a tier gets quietly shrunk back.

*** SPRINT 74 / V0.29.29 -- US-539 DONE (commit f48b3c6). 1 of 6. Next up: US-540-a (set the scale VALUES 44/34/26/20/15), which US-539 was the hard prereq for. ***

THE STORY HAD A CONTRADICTION IN ITS OWN ACCEPTANCE AND I RESOLVED IT RATHER THAN BLOCKING -- READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING US-540. AC3 asks for BOTH a five-token scale AND 'dashboard renders visually identical'. dashboard.css shipped 82 bare `font-size: Npx` over 15 DISTINCT values (8/9/10/11/12/13/14/15/17/18/20/22/30/34/40). Fifteen values do not fit in five slots, so the two clauses are mutually exclusive ON THIS FILE. I took the COLLAPSE. The decisive argument was not aesthetics, it was the NEXT STORY: the pixel-identical design (5 tokens + ~10 extra tokens holding the off-scale sizes) BREAKS US-540-a, which is specified as setting FIVE values and would leave ten stale -- the exact 'edits that drift' problem the story exists to kill, just smaller. Filed as offices/pm/issues/I-us539-type-scale-collapse-is-not-pixel-identical.md with the full movement table; PM/Iris owe a ratify, and US-539's validationCriteria wants amending ('nothing renders smaller; hierarchy preserved' is the honest gate).

*** THE GENERALIZABLE LESSON: when two acceptance clauses conflict, do not pick by which sentence reads louder -- pick by WHICH READING LETS THE NEXT STORY BE BUILT AS WRITTEN. That test resolved it in one step where re-reading the clauses had me going in circles for a while. ***

AS BUILT: --fs-hero/primary/secondary/label/meta declared in specs/UI/tokens.css and MIRRORED into dashboard.css :root at the PRE-F-127 shipped values 40/20/14/12/10. The mirror is not laziness -- dashboard.html links ONLY dashboard.css, so an SSOT-only drop leaves the panel unsized with a fully green suite (BL-027's lesson, same file, one token family later). Every off-scale rule rounds UP to its tier: NOTHING on the panel got smaller. 34/30/22->hero(3), 18/17/15->primary(6), 13->secondary(21), 11->label(14), 9/8->meta(3); 35 rules already sat on a scale value. US-540-a is now literally 5 value edits x 2 files.

WATCH THIS ONE ON HARDWARE: the STOP takeover directive moved 22->40px. Forced, not chosen -- Spool 6d requires it outrank its base rule (.takeover-directive, which landed on primary), and collapsing both onto primary turns a SAFETY guard red. 'PULL OVER NOW' at 40px mono is ~340px of the 442px available, so it fits on paper; US-540-a raises hero to 44 ON TOP OF THIS, so EYEBALL IT during the in-car acceptance.

*** ADOPT THIS WHEN A REFACTOR CHANGES HOW A VALUE IS SPELLED: FIND EVERY TEST THAT PARSES THE OLD SPELLING FIRST. Two PRE-EXISTING guards read font sizes with a raw-px regex, and BOTH are safety guards (STOP directive > base; DTC detail directive > base copy). After tokenization one would have died on a None match and the other would have silently compared -1 -- a refactor that blinds a safety guard is worse than the drift it fixed. `grep -rn 'font-size' tests/` took ten seconds and found both. They now resolve var(--fs-*) through the scale via ONE shared helper, tests/ui/css_type_scale.py. ***

SUBTLE TRAP, COST ME A RED: ruleBlock() MUST be line-anchored. A plain `css.index('.takeover-directive {')` finds the STOP OVERRIDE `#dtc-takeover[data-severity="stop"] .takeover-directive {` first, because it is declared EARLIER in the sheet -- so a guard meant to compare an override against its base compares the override against ITSELF and reports 40 > 40 as a passing hierarchy. My first cut had exactly that bug; the pre-existing suite had already solved it (test_dashboard_stop_tier_safety::_ruleBlock, anchored `^`), which is why only MY new test went red. The anchored version now lives in the shared helper.

NEW GATE tests/ui/test_dashboard_type_scale.py (17 tests). Every assertion is an ABSENCE check, so it ships with a NEGATIVE CONTROL: the bare-px detector runs against a stylesheet that DOES carry drift and must report it, and against `--fs-hero: 40px` where it must NOT fire. Without that pair a typo in the pattern reads as a green gate over a file full of literals (same shape as US-550's Grep blindspot and US-545's PYTHONPATH dict-key miss -- an empty result is evidence ONLY once you know the lookup can see the thing). Also gated: font-size RHS is only a scale token or the deliberate `inherit` on .detail-value (US-491 load-bearing -- binding a token there re-breaks the tier ramp and looks tidier doing it); no SIXTH --fs-* token; scale strictly descending, asserted as ORDER not numbers so it survives US-540-a.
